nonPoolDecisions: Reading: all ten questions are required; each printed (a)/(b) part is a 5-mark practice card. “3 mharc + 2 mharc” items are order-dependent (first correct point 3, second 2) and stay whole at 0/3/5; single answers with a printed partial (“= 3 mharc”) allow 0/3/5, otherwise 0/5.
Reading language: “Gaeilge lochtach: 0 - 5 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh” is one deduction from each 50-mark passage total; cards state it without applying it inside a part.

Prescribed prose (2A): Dís (a) and Oisín i dTír na nÓg (b) each print five 5-mark sub-questions: each whole option is a 25-mark card and every sub-question is also a practice card (“3 mharc + 2 mharc” sub-questions keep 0/3/5). 2A(c) is a choose-one between two texts: Cáca Milis and An Lasair Choille are separate 25-mark cards (different topics).

Prescribed poetry (3A): each poem is a whole 25-mark card with (i) 8, (ii) 8, (iii) 9 and one 0–4 Gaeilge deduction; every printed sub-question is also a practice card. 3A(b)(i) prints four 2-mark questions (a)–(d): each is a practice slot (0/2).
Literature mark values: other literature sub-questions keep the full range because the scheme’s points are indicative and further relevant points are credited “de réir a bhfiúntais”.

Optional prose (2B) and optional poetry (3B) stay whole: the text is open content chosen by the candidate. 2B(c) film or play shares one grid and one topic, so it stays one card with both printed alternatives.

Choose-two within 2A, 2B, 3A or 3B is a choice, not a route: each printed option keeps its own card and carries the instruction in its task requirements; no combination cards. The scheme marks each option on its own (no joint marking).
Q2A or Q2B and Q3A or Q3B are alternatives; scheme lists of sample answers are indicative answer keys, not route pools.
The modified marking scheme (PDF 33) changes language assessment for eligible candidates, not the printed tasks.
caveats: Paper 2 = 200: Léamhthuiscint A 50 + B 50 (five questions of 10, each (a) 5 + (b) 5), Prós 50 (two of three at 25), Filíocht 50 (two of three at 25).
Reading A “Oileán agus Ionad an Bhlascaoid Mhóir” (paper pages 4–5, scheme PDF 15–16) and B “Mearfhaisean” (paper 6–7, scheme PDF 17–18).

Prescribed prose (paper 8): Dís (i)–(v) and Oisín i dTír na nÓg (i)–(v) at 5 each; Cáca Milis or An Lasair Choille one 25-mark question (five points at 2 + 3). Optional prose (paper 9): (a) theme 1 + 22 + title/author 2; (b) naming 1 + 22 + title 2; (c) film or play 23 (5,5,5,4,4) + title/writer 2.

Prescribed poetry (paper 10–12): Colscaradh, An Spailpín Fánach ((i) four 2-mark questions), Géibheann at 8/8/9. Optional poetry (paper 13): (a) 9 (5 + 4) / 7 (1 + 3 + 3) / 7, (b) 9 (1 + 4 + 4) / 7 / 7, (c) 9 / 7 / 7, + 2 for poem and poet; the same poem may not be used twice.
Literature language: “[Gaeilge lochtach: 0-4 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh]” after every literature answer; it is a deduction from that answer, never inside one sub-question.

The legacy cards marked every literature answer as one 25-mark Eolas block and every reading question as one 10-mark block; the 2A(c) card carried both texts. They now carry the printed part and sub-question tariffs, and 2A(c) is Cáca Milis.

taskRequirements: Freagair do rogha dhá cheann as (a), (b) nó (c).

criteria.label: Eolas
guidance: (iii) Cén saghas duine é an spailpín, dar leat? Tabhair dhá fháth, i d’fhocail féin, le do fhreagra. (9 marc) An saghas duine = 1 mharc Dhá fháth = 4 mharc + 4 mharc An saghas duine: Bródúil…láidir…oibrí maith…brónach…díoltasach…dóchasach…grá dá thír... Fáthanna samplacha: • Tá sé brónach mar níl aon obair aige agus bíonn sé tinn go minic… • Tá sé láidir mar rachaidh sé ag troid… • Tá sé díoltasach mar is fuath leis na Sasanaigh…

Nóta: Níl sé i gceist a chur in iúl go bhfuil na freagraí samplacha thíos uileghabhálach ná eisiach. Is samplaí de fhreagraí féideartha atá iontu; déanfaidh na scrúdaitheoirí tuillteanas gach freagra a mheas agus bronnfar marcanna ar phointí bailí eolais eile a chuirfidh na hiarrthóirí i láthair de réir a bhfiúntais.
